s: Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is
x: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha at 250, comprising 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated members.
tq: Distinguish the constitutional maximum from the present strength.

s: The present composition of the Rajya Sabha is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 7 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 12 representatives of Union Territories and 8 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members
233 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated members
x: The present strength is 245: 225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members.
tq: Separate present composition from the constitutional maximum.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the election of representatives of States to the Rajya Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. They are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
2. The election is held by proportional representation through the single transferable vote system.
3. Nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in this election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Article 80(4). Nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in this election.
tq: Check the elector and the voting method separately; the nominated-member statement is the trap.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: The allocation of seats to the States in the Rajya Sabha is provided in the
x: The Fourth Schedule specifies the allocation of seats in the Council of States to the States and Union Territories.
tq: Use the exact constitutional Schedule rather than the subject-matter Schedules.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: Rajya Sabha seats are allocated to States primarily on the basis of
x: Seats in the Rajya Sabha are allocated broadly according to population under the Fourth Schedule and Article 80(2).
tq: Apply the comparison with the United States Senate: Indian States do not have equal representation.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: The term of office of a member of the Rajya Sabha is
x: A Rajya Sabha member serves for six years. The House itself is not subject to dissolution.
tq: Separate the individual member’s term from the continuing nature of the House.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s:
The qualification for nomination to the Rajya Sabha includes special knowledge or practical experience in which of the following fields?
1. Literature
2. Science
3. Art
4. Social service
5. Sports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Article 80(3) mentions literature, science, art and social service. Sports is not one of the four constitutionally listed fields.
tq: Identify the exact constitutional list and exclude the look-alike addition.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: The President may nominate how many members to the Rajya Sabha?
x: Twelve members may be nominated to the Rajya Sabha from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in the specified fields.
tq: Distinguish the number nominated to the Rajya Sabha from the former Anglo-Indian provision in the Lok Sabha.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: A nominated member of the Rajya Sabha may join a political party without attracting disqualification within
o: one year of taking the seat
six months of taking the seat
the entire duration of the first session
three months of taking the seat
x: A nominated member may join a political party within six months of taking the seat. Joining after that period attracts disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
tq: Watch the precise time limit in a disqualification rule.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements regarding nominated members of the Rajya Sabha is correct?
o: They may take full part in debates and can vote in the Vice-Presidential election, but not in the Presidential election.
They cannot participate in debates but may vote on Money Bills.
They are barred from voting in every election held by Parliament.
They can vote in the Presidential election but not in the Vice-Presidential election.
x: Nominated Rajya Sabha members can participate fully in debates and vote in the election of the Vice-President, but they cannot vote in the election of the President.
tq: Discriminate between the Presidential and Vice-Presidential electoral colleges.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding nominated members of the Rajya Sabha:
1. Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012.
2. Mary Kom was nominated in 2016.
3. Lata Mangeshkar was nominated for her contribution to sport.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 and Mary Kom in 2016. Lata Mangeshkar represented the field of art, not sport.
tq: Match notable persons with the correct field and avoid the swapped-domain trap.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s:
The Supreme Court decision in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006) upheld which of the following in relation to Rajya Sabha elections?
1. Removal of the domicile requirement
2. Use of an open ballot
3. Direct election by all citizens of the State
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Supreme Court upheld the removal of the domicile requirement and the open-ballot system. Rajya Sabha members are not directly elected by all citizens of a State.
tq: Separate the two holdings of the judgment from the constitutionally prescribed electoral method.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of their Rajya Sabha representation:
A. Tamil Nadu
B. Maharashtra
C. Uttar Pradesh
D. West Bengal
x: The correct order is Uttar Pradesh (31), Maharashtra (19), West Bengal (16) and Tamil Nadu (18) — wait, numerically Tamil Nadu has 18 and therefore must precede West Bengal. Thus the correct descending order is Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal.
tq: Arrange numerical values carefully rather than relying on name familiarity.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following States has the highest number of seats in the Rajya Sabha?
x: Uttar Pradesh has the highest Rajya Sabha representation among the States, with 31 seats.
tq: Use the largest-value comparison in the representation table.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following groups consists only of States having one seat each in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Tripura
x: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura each have one Rajya Sabha seat. The group in option a contains only such States.
tq: Check every member of the group against the single-seat condition.
sec: Rajya Sabha - strength, election, retirement, Fourth Schedule, nominated members  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 81, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is
x: Article 81 provides for a maximum of 550 members in the Lok Sabha: 530 from the States and 20 from the Union Territories.
tq: Distinguish the present constitutional maximum from the older figure that included nominated Anglo-Indians.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: The present strength of the Lok Sabha is composed of
o: 530 members from States and 13 from Union Territories
524 members from States and 19 from Union Territories
525 members from States and 18 from Union Territories
x: The present strength is 543, comprising 524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories.
tq: Split the total into its State and Union Territory components.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the maximum and present strength of the Lok Sabha?
x: The constitutional maximum is 550, while the present strength is 543. The older figure of 552 included two nominated Anglo-Indian members.
tq: Compare the current figure with the historical figure instead of treating them as interchangeable.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: The nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha under Article 331 was discontinued by the
x: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 ended the provision for nomination of up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha, with effect from 25 January 2020.
tq: Pair the constitutional provision with the correct amendment and effective date.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: Prior to its discontinuance, Article 331 enabled the President to nominate up to how many Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha?
x: Article 331 permitted the President to nominate up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha if the community was not adequately represented.
tq: Distinguish the former nomination limit from the present elected strength.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: The allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha to the States remains frozen on the basis of the 1971 Census until
o: the completion of the 2031 Census only
x: The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026.
tq: Read the endpoint of a constitutional freeze precisely.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements regarding delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies is correct?
o: The allocation and constituencies were both permanently frozen by the 84th Amendment.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 1971 Census by the Election Commission.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 2001 Census by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 2011 Census by Parliament alone.
x: The 87th Amendment enabled readjustment of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 Census. This work was undertaken by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.
tq: Distinguish freezing seat allocation from readjusting constituency boundaries.
sec: Lok Sabha - maximum and present strength, seats by State, Anglo-Indians  [APPSC]

s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched with the number of Lok Sabha seats?
1. Andhra Pradesh — 25
2. Telangana — 17
3. Uttarakhand — 5
4. Jammu and Kashmir — 5
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairs are correct: Andhra Pradesh has 25, Telangana 17, Uttarakhand 5 and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir 5 Lok Sabha seats.
tq: Verify each numerical pair independently before choosing the coded combination.

s: Which one of the following States has exactly one Lok Sabha seat?
x: Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland each have one Lok Sabha seat. Tripura, Goa and Meghalaya have more than one.
tq: Do not confuse States with one Rajya Sabha seat and States with one Lok Sabha seat.

Which of the following Union Territories has one Lok Sabha seat?
1. Andaman and Nicobar Islands

3. Lakshadweep
4. Ladakh
5. Puducherry
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

tq: Check the complete list rather than stopping after the first familiar examples.
